headline: PCB Raw Material Costs Surge Across the Supply Chain in Q1 2026
body: Multiple PCB material suppliers announced price increases in Q1 2026, with copper clad laminate and copper foil leading the wave.
Mitsui Kinzoku notified customers on March 12 of a 12% price increase on all MicroThin copper foil products, effective April 20, 2026.
Mitsubishi Gas Chemical raised prices by 30% on laminate and prepreg materials.
LME copper crossed $13,300 per tonne in January 2026, more than 20% above the late 2025 average.
insight: Simultaneous price increases across copper foil, glass fabric, resins, and CCL signal a structural cost shift, not a temporary spike.
caption:
27%. That is how much of every PCB's cost comes from one material: copper clad laminate.
In Q1 2026, that material just got significantly more expensive.
Mitsui Kinzoku announced a 12% price increase on all MicroThin copper foil, effective April 20.
Mitsubishi Gas Chemical raised laminate and prepreg prices by 30%.
LME copper crossed $13,300 per tonne in January 2026, more than 20% above late 2025 levels.
Glass fabric capacity in Japan and Taiwan is being redirected toward low Dk yarns for AI server boards, tightening supply for standard laminates.
This is not one commodity spiking. It is copper foil, glass cloth, epoxy resins, and CCL all moving up at the same time.
Analysts describe this as structural, not cyclical.
For PCB buyers, the math is simple: CCL accounts for 27.31% of the total board cost. When CCL rises, every layer of a multilayer design costs more.
With next generation M9 materials scaling in 2027, high end PCB prices are projected to rise a further 30% to 50%.
How is your supply chain preparing for this?
